# UE5 animation event schema (generated by tools/export_unreal_data.py from anim_events.js)

Status: NOT consumed by any Unreal code yet. Unreal is not installed on this PC; the JSON was generated by running `anim_events.js` under Node.
Purpose: lets an Unreal AnimInstance / event dispatcher listen to the same event ids the sim already emits (AE(player, kind, payload)).

## Priority classes (higher wins)

cancel=200, fall=100, victim=92, save=90, contact=80, foul=78, release=75, windup=70, gpoke=66, cover=60, react=55, recv=50, bench=45, misc=30, celebrate=20, idle=10

## Interruption rules (verbatim from anim_events.js)

- fall interrupts everything (including check recovery) except a fall already in its first 0.35 s
- checked / check interrupt skating, carrying and receiving; a victim animation is not restarted while the fall is running
- a shot or pass release (t < contact) cannot be interrupted except by fall, checked or actcancel (the sim cancels with actcancel)
- while a fall is running only fall events start (nothing plays on a skater who is on the ice)
- while a celebration or dejection runs only fall starts; celebration only starts once the goal is confirmed
- goalie save interrupts ready, idle, play, peek, poke and bench; goalagainst never cuts a running save
- goalie cover is deferred until the save animation ends (route)
- incompatible layers never overlap on one player: fall x event, celebration x event, bench trip x save

## Goalie event kinds

save, cover, goalagainst, poke, pull, return, idle, pump, peek, play

## Files

Content/Data/AnimEvents.json (full table: events, priorities, rules, dedupe, goalie kinds) and AnimEvents.csv (FLihlAnimEventRow).

## Notes
- `celebrate`, `dejected`, `win` are state-driven in the web game (p.celeb), not discrete events; an Unreal port should emit them explicitly.
- `poke_g` is sent by the sim as kind `poke` on the goalie; anim_goalie maps it. The table lists it separately with class gpoke.
